title: terraform: private-deploy modules - GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking, and state layout
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Private deployments need a robust, repeatable Terraform module layout to provision GPU node pools, explicit IAM roles/policies, VPC/networking, and a clearer remote state layout to enable multi-region and environment isolation. This PR introduces: consolidated GPU node pool module with taints/labels and autoscaling configs; explicit IAM role/policy modules for node pools and KMS access; networking module tweaks to support private subnets for control plane + worker separation; and a new remote state key layout + migration guide to reduce chance of destructive diffs during upgrades.

What changed (high-level):
- modules/gpu-node-pool: new module for GPU-backed node pools with configurable machine types, accelerator count, node taints, labels, and autoscaling parameters. Adds feature flags for GKE/AWS EKS differences and an explicit rollout strategy resource for controlled node replacement.
- modules/iam: new modularized IAM role and policy templates for node pools, KMS key access, and image pull secrets (min-privilege by default).
- modules/networking: private-subnet support for control-plane-only traffic, optional egress NAT gateways, and improved tagging for firewall/security group rules.
- backend/state-layout: changed remote state key scheme to <org>/<env>/<region>/<component>.tfstate and helpers to move existing state into new keys.
- examples/private-deployments: updated example usage and a migration-runbook.

Checklist (implemented):
- [x] GPU node pool module with unit tests and example usage
- [x] IAM role/policy templates and least-priv privilege defaults
- [x] Networking updates and example configs for private control plane + worker subnets
- [x] Remote state layout + migration helpers + runbook
- [x] Integration tests against a staging Private environment (see testing notes)

Notes on backwards compatibility / upgrade impact:
- The new remote state key layout is a breaking operational change to how we name backend keys; code changes attempt to avoid resource recreation, but operators must follow the migration runbook to move existing state keys. The PR provides terraform state mv commands and a helper script under scripts/state-migrate.sh.
- GPU node pool resource addresses were namespaced under the new module path; the migration guide includes exact terraform state mv commands to preserve existing resources.

Testing performed:
- Local terraform validate and fmt across modules
- Unit tests for modules using terraform-compliance style assertions (CI)
- End-to-end apply in staging (private-deploy-staging-us-west1) with a single GPU node pool and traffic smoke tests; validated that pod scheduling with GPU taints works and IAM role bindings are correct.
- CI run with full module matrix (aws/gcp) passing on rerun after initial flakey gcp-network test was fixed.

Related work:
- ENG-4521 (Private deploy infra refactor)
- ENG-4599 (GPU autoscaler improvements)

Release notes:
Updated Terraform modules for Private deployments: adds GPU node-pool module, modular IAM roles/policies, networking improvements for private control plane deployments, and a new remote state layout. Operators must follow the migration runbook before upgrading existing deployments to avoid drift or resource re-creation.

changes_summary: modules/gpu-node-pool/main.tf: new module to create GPU-enabled node pools (configurable accel_count, machine_type, taints, labels, autoscaling). Added lifecycle.prefer_destroy = false and create_before_destroy where applicable to reduce downtime.
modules/iam/roles.tf: new IAM roles for node pools and KMS access; least-privilege policies and role assumption docs. Added variable for external_id to support cross-account scenarios.
modules/networking/main.tf: private_subnets boolean and additional route/nat configuration; security-group rules tightened for control-plane to worker traffic only.

backend/remote_state_layout.tf: changed backend key template to "${var.org}/${var.environment}/${var.region}/${var.component}.tfstate" and provided helper script scripts/state-migrate.sh to migrate existing keys.
examples/private-deployments/staging.tfvars: sample values for staging env using new modules
scripts/state-migrate.sh: helper to automate terraform state mv operations (dry-run by default).
tests/integration/gpu-smoke-test.sh: test asserting GPU taints/labels and basic pod scheduling on a test cluster.

upgrade_instructions:
IMPORTANT: follow the migration runbook in examples/private-deployments/MIGRATION.md before applying module changes to existing environments. Summary steps:
1) Backup current remote state (download current .tfstate file).
2) Run scripts/state-migrate.sh --dry-run to see proposed terraform state mv commands.
3) When ready, run scripts/state-migrate.sh --apply which performs terraform state mv from old keys to new keys (example: terraform state mv 'module.old_gpu.module.node_pool.aws_eks_node_group.main[0]' 'module.gpu_node_pool.aws_eks_node_group.main[0]').
4) terraform init -reconfigure with the new backend configuration.
5) terraform plan: confirm no planned resource replacements.
6) Apply in staging first; then roll out to production.
If you are using a CI-managed remote state (S3/GCS), ensure the pipeline has permissions to perform state operations and that locking is enabled during migration.
release_notes: New terraform modules for Private deployments: GPU node pools, explicit IAM roles/policies, improved private networking support, and a new remote state key layout. Operators must follow provided migration runbook to avoid resource re-creation.
